Subject: SOW & pricing for Q2 prompt-eval labeling engagement

Hi Aisha / LabelWorks team,

Hope you're well — we're preparing our Q2 evals and want to lock a labeling partner for prompt-evaluation work (prompt-based rubric, multi-annotator adjudication). High level: ~100k items over 3 months, mixed complexity (simple classification ~60%, multi-turn QA ~30%, edge-case adjudication ~10%). Primary asks:
- Estimated per-label rate and tiered pricing for 10k / 50k / 100k volumes
- SLA / turnaround for each tier (typical target: 48–72h for bulk batches)
- Data handling: SOC2, subprocessor list, and proposed retention/deletion policy
- Sample SOW and a proposed timeline for ramp and pilot

Attached is our scope sheet to help — redwood_evals_scope_2026-03.xlsx (sample schema + required QA metrics). Can you send an updated SOW and ballpark pricing by EOD next Tue (Mar 3)? We're aiming to start a pilot the week of Mar 15.

Thanks — looping Marissa to help with commercial details.

Jordan Blake

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the scope — great to see the schema. We can support the mix you outlined. High level estimate below and attached SOW (LW_SOW_v1.pdf):

Pricing (USD) — net of discounts:
- Pilot (10k items): $0.48 / unit (reduced pilot rate)
- 50k band: $0.62 / unit
- 100k band: $0.56 / unit (volume discount)

Notes:
- We price 'unit' as one labeled judgment (with adjudication counted as an extra unit per item when used).
- Turnaround: 48–72h for continuous batches at 50k+/mo.
- Quality: target inter-annotator agreement (IAA) 0.82+; we include a 3% rework allowance in scope.
- Data handling: we are SOC2 Type II compliant; we provide subprocessor list on request and can agree to a 60-day retention window by default.

I've attached LW_SOW_v1.pdf with scope, timelines, and standard T&Cs. A few legal/Commercial flags to note up front: we use a standard liability cap (12 months' fees) and limited warranty; IP assignment language is our standard for labels (we license annotation outputs to the customer). If you want different terms we can discuss redlines.

If you're open to it, we can run a reduced pilot week of Mar 15 (10k) at the pilot rate to validate schema and throughput.

Best,

Thanks for the loop. Quick summary of redlines / outstanding items from Legal and Risk: 
- Retention: prefer 30 days after project close; if LabelWorks insists on longer, need explicit purpose and strong controls.
- IP & Outputs: prefer assignment of labeling outputs to Redwood (or an exclusive license) for our internal model training; LabelWorks' draft licenses outputs which is acceptable only if perpetual exclusive license is granted to us.
- Liability cap: 12 months' fees is borderline — need to reduce to 6 months for labeling work given data sensitivity.
- Subprocessors: require prior notice of new subprocessors and right to object for any that handle raw data.
- SLA credits: define clear KPIs (batch turnaround, IAA thresholds) and credits/termination triggers for missed SLAs.

Attached: SOW_redlines_eh_20260308.pdf (redlined SOW + comment summary). Please review with Procurement/Finance for PO/commit process. Priyom — can you confirm Redwood's purchasing timeline and PO lead times? Vivek — confirm feasibility of 48–72h SLA and the proposed IAA target; if we need more overlap for adjudication, flag that.

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the clear redlines. I've run these past our legal and ops teams — summary response below and an updated SOW attached (Updated_SOW_v3.pdf).

What we can accept: 
- Retention: we can commit to a 30-day deletion window for raw data with certified deletion logs provided on request.
- IP: we can amend to grant Redwood a perpetual, exclusive, worldwide license to the annotation outputs for training and internal use (we reserve the right to use anonymized aggregate metrics).
- Subprocessors: we will provide the current list and commit to 15 days' prior notice for new ones; critical subprocessors will be listed in Appendix A.
- SLA credits: acceptable — propose a credit matrix (in SOW) tied to missed batch SLA and IAA < 0.78.

What we cannot accept without exec signoff:
- Liability cap: we typically hold to 12 months' fees; to move to 6 months we'd need exec approval. As a compromise, we can offer a 9-month cap and a 5% discount on unit pricing for a 12-month committed term.

Commercial proposal: run the 10k pilot at the pilot rate ($0.48/unit) the week of Mar 15. If pilot passes QA, commit to a 12-month engagement at $0.52/unit for 100k+ volumes with the 5% commit discount reflected in the SOW.

Next steps: I can send the updated SOW to DocuSign once we align on the cap and pilot. Also including a DocuSign link placeholder.

Best,
Aisha Fernandez
Head of Operations | LabelWorks
aisha@labelworks.ai
